svg.title: Pass dependency diagrams
svg.desc: Twelve diagrams explain terrain dependencies, edge discovery, access hazards, registration order, culling, queue flow, and the external back buffer root.

g.title: Full terrain producer and synchronization graph
g.desc: GraphPrologue produces the external upload buffer and BackBuffer. Upload, generate, erode, triangulate, render, and overlay form the live producer chain. DebugHeightmap is dead and has an ordering-only synchronization edge to ErodeHeightmap.

g.title: Read-to-write synchronization edge
g.desc: A pass reading the old value must finish before a later pass writes the new value. The synchronization edge orders them without carrying culling liveness.
g.text: A later write must not overtake an earlier read
May still be culled if unobservable
Cannot execute before a live reader
Used for levels and queue waits; ignored by backward culling

g.title: Edge discovery flowchart
g.desc: For each access, add an edge from the last producer if valid. A read is remembered. A write receives synchronization edges from readers, clears readers, and becomes the last producer.
g.text: One resource history record discovers both edge kinds
If lastProducer is valid, add producer edge
History remains on the same version

g.title: Read-after-write trace
g.desc: P2 writes Heightmap and becomes the last producer. P3 reads Heightmap, receives a producer edge from P2, and joins the readers set.
g.text: RAW: the reader depends on the latest writer
The producer edge carries both ordering and data-flow liveness

g.title: Write-after-write trace
g.desc: P2 writes Heightmap and becomes last producer. P4 then writes Heightmap, receives a producer edge from P2, and replaces P2 as last producer.
g.text: WAW: the later writer extends the version chain
Repeated UAV use may also require a UAV barrier
The dependency edge and resource barrier solve different ordering layers

g.title: Write-after-read trace
g.desc: P3 reads the version produced by P2 and joins readers. P4 also depends on P2, receives a synchronization edge from P3, clears readers, and becomes the last producer.
g.text: WAR: preserve the old version until its readers finish
Culling ignores the sync edge, so an otherwise dead P3 does not become live

g.title: Extracted two-pass chain and dead branch
g.desc: GenerateNoiseHeightmap produces both TriangulateTerrain and DebugHeightmap. TriangulateTerrain produces the extracted terrain mesh observed by GraphEpilogue. DebugHeightmap has no path to a root and is culled.
g.text: Extraction gives the useful branch a path to the epilogue
Backward traversal reaches Generate through Triangulate, but not Debug

g.title: Correct and incorrect pass registration order
g.desc: Correct registration adds producer P1 before consumer P2. Incorrect registration adds the consumer first and expects compilation to move a later producer before it, which compilation does not do.
g.text: Registration order must already be topological
Compile does not reorder the registry
After culling, execution is registry order with dead passes removed

g.title: Backward culling reachability tree
g.desc: Culling starts from GraphEpilogue and NeverCull roots, then walks backward through producer edges. Synchronization producers are not visited.
g.text: Culling walks backward from observable roots
Only producer reachability changes a pass from culled to live

g.title: Terrain culling live chain
g.desc: Generate, Erode, Triangulate, Render, and Overlay form a live producer chain ending at GraphEpilogue through BackBuffer. DebugHeightmap reads the version from Generate and has an ordering-only edge to Erode, but remains culled.
g.text: The observable BackBuffer keeps the terrain chain live
BackBuffer is the external observable output
A synchronization-only connection from Debug to Erode cannot rescue Debug

g.title: Terrain pipeline queue lane
g.desc: UploadTerrainSettings runs on Copy, GenerateNoiseHeightmap, ErodeHeightmap, and TriangulateTerrain run on AsyncCompute, and RenderTerrain and TerrainOverlay run on Graphics.
g.text: The live terrain declaration crosses three GPU queues
Dependency levels and queue instances derive waits where the chain crosses lanes

g.title: External BackBuffer root
g.desc: GraphPrologue supplies the imported BackBuffer in Present state to RenderTerrain. RenderTerrain writes it as a render target, and GraphEpilogue observes and returns it to Present state.
g.text: An external swap-chain write is naturally observable
